title: `podman run` fails with WSL v3.0.1
body:
### Issue Description

The following error is returned when trying `podman run hello` on the latest version of WSL (v3.0.1):

```pwsh
> podman run hello 
Error: preparing container 175dfadfb2db1773aaeb9f82994a347e7fd0d8bff927d5223b5bd65f5e905017 for attach: crun: 
controller `pids` is not available under /sys/fs/cgroup/wsl-user/distro-440/user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/user.slice/libpod-175dfadfb2db1773aaeb9f82994a347e7fd0d8bff927d5223b5bd65f5e905017.scope/container/cgroup.controllers: OCI runtime error
```

##### 🟢 Workaround 1: use `--cgroups disabled`

```pwsh
podman run --cgroups=disabled hello
```

##### 🟢 Workaround 2: set `cgroup_manager="cgroupfs"` in containers.conf

```pwsh
Add-Content -Path "$env:APPDATA\containers\containers.conf" -Value "[engine]`ncgroup_manager=`"cgroupfs`"" -NoNewLine
```

### Steps to reproduce the issue

Steps to reproduce the issue
1. wsl --update # <-- this installs version 3.0.1
2. podman machine init --now
3. podman run hello

comments.body:
This happens even though pids is correctly delegated at every level above the container's own leaf cgroup:
 - Root `cgroup.subtree_control: cpuset cpu io memory hugetlb pids rdma` (includes `pids`)
 - `/etc/systemd/system/user@.service.d/delegate.conf` (shipped by default in the machine image): `Delegate=memory pids cpu io` (includes `pids`)
 - Intermediate `user.slice` / `user-1000.slice` / `user@1000.service` levels: `pids` present

Despite this, the transient `libpod-<id>.scope/container` cgroup crun creates for the container ends up with an empty `cgroup.controllers` file — no pids, even though the immediate parent should be delegating it.

Behavior is inconsistent across images: a plain `alpine sleep 600` container sometimes starts successfully, while `openbao/openbao` fails consistently.

Spend couple of hours on this, ended up starting my container with `--cgroups=disabled`.

> everything was freshly installed
also have this bug on Windows amd64, with WSL 2.9.11. the image is ghcr.io/pnpm/pnpm

I just hit this after clean-upgrading from 5.8.2 to 6.1.1. I got the same error text, same kernel (`6.18.40.1-1`), but on WSL 2.9.8.0 rather than the 2.9.11 pre-release, and on x64 rather than ARM64.

Setting `cgroup_manager = "cgroupfs"` was a WSL-specific workaround baked into `/etc/containers/containers.conf` at machine-init time (see the `containersConf` const in `pkg/machine/wsl/declares.go`, pre-6.0). With `cgroupfs`, podman never asks systemd to create a transient scope, so the WSL delegation gap above never gets hit. That override was removed in `81fd1e6e` ("machine/wsl: drop cgroup_manager cgroupfs"), which shipped between `v6.0.0-rc1` and `v6.0.0`.

The problem seems to be that nothing seeds `%APPDATA%\containers` with defaults, so the default cgroup manager falls through to `systemd`.

Thus, it seems to me that any fresh `machine init` on the WSL provider from 6.0.0 onward is just broken.

*Workarounds that fixed it for me*, for anyone hitting this before (presumably) a fix happens:
- Per-run: `podman run --cgroups=disabled ...`
- Persistent: manually add `cgroup_manager = "cgroupfs"` under `[engine]` in `%APPDATA%\containers\containers.conf`

I'm happy to share more diagnostic detail if useful.

The root cause is that in WSL 2.9.x, the podman-machine distribution cgroups sit in a `non-systemd` subtree, along with cgroups for other processes such as WSLg that belong to the WSL root namespace. This prevents the cgroup controllers from propagating when a container starts. More info [here](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/41492).

Using `cgroup_manager=cgroupfs` is a valid workaround, and [I have opened a PR to make it the default for WSL](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman-machine-os/pull/319), but it disables cgroups in rootless mode (the default) and this is not ideal. We should eventually [document](https://docs.podman.io/en/stable/markdown/podman.1.html#cgroup-manager-manager) this.

The clean solution is to use [the built-in WSL systemd support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/systemd), but that requires changes to our code. I verified that, in that case, the pids controller is correctly propagated with WSL 2.9.x, and [I opened a draft PR to run CI checks](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29837).
It's not pre-release anymore. WSL 3.0.1 is out today. I'm running into this issue.

# TL;DR;

Persistent workaround isn't working around for me. Am I doing something wrong, or am I just out of luck? When is this fix likely to be deployed? 

# Summary

I have also hit this issue, after having updated WSL to 3.0.1.0. However, the "persistent" workaround doesn't seem to be working for me. I have created the `containers` file and added the suggested snippet, as seen below:
```
$: echo $APPDATA
/c/Users/Eric Liebowitz/AppData/Roaming/
$: pwd
/c/Users/Eric Liebowitz/AppData/Roaming/containers
$: cat containers.conf
[engine]
cgroup_manager="cgroupfs"
```

After having created this file, I restarted my computer, removed and re-initialized my podman machine w/ the following:
```
$: podman machine stop
$: podman machine rm
$: podman machine init
$: podman machine set --rootful
$: podman machine start
```

When I attempt to run the `hello` container, it fails w/ the aforementioned error:

@LeboyX, I suspect your configuration file is being ignored. Please run this command from a PowerShell terminal:

```pwsh
(podman info -f json | ConvertFrom-Json).host.cgroupManager
```

If it doesn't return `cgroupfs`, it confirms that it is ignored. You need to check whether the configuration file gets mounted in the podman machine with this second command:

```pwsh
podman machine ssh cat /etc/containers/containers.conf
```

@LeboyX, I have been able to reproduce your problem. The conf file doesn't get mounted when the username has a space. I am providing a fix for that too.

As a workaround (the 3rd!), you can

```pwsh
podman machine ssh --username root 'mkdir -p /usr/share/containers/containers.conf.d/'
podman machine ssh --username root 'printf "[engine]\ncgroup_manager=\"cgroupfs\"\n" > /usr/share/containers/containers.conf.d/999-podman-machine-wsl-cgroupfs.conf'
```

This persists until you remove the machine.

# TL;DR;

Steps followed and work as expected. Problem worked-around. Thanks so much, @l0rd!

Edit --
Seems like since I was mapping ports to the windows loopback `127.0.0.1:8080:8080`, now the service is only bound to the podman-machine's loopback.  removing the IP makes it accessible on the podman-machine's IP as well from windows, but still does not bind it to any windows IPs.

@LeboyX Podman Desktop configures the machine in Rootful mode and the instructions I have provided only work when the machine is configured in Rootless mode. My bad. Use the following command to make it work for both Rootful and Rootless:

```pwsh
podman machine ssh --username root 'mkdir -p /usr/share/containers/containers.conf.d/'
podman machine ssh --username root 'printf "[engine]\ncgroup_manager=\"cgroupfs\"\n" > /usr/share/containers/containers.conf.d/999-podman-machine-wsl-cgroupfs.conf'
```

> I believe that the design is that containers.conf in ~/.config/containers will get mounted into your podman machine wsl image. It seems from discussion here that sometimes it doesn't.

@pelaxa folder `%APPDATA%/containers` gets mounted into the Podman machine, not `~/.config/containers`. And because of a bug (thanks @LeboyX for finding this out), that folder doesn't get mounted if the `%APPDATA%` has spaces (for example, `C:\Users\John Doe\AppData\Roaming`). This bug is also addressed by [this PR](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/pull/29883).
